list: The official 55 trophies, as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles on 2026-11-18 (the two agreeing on every name, description and grade). Names and descriptions are shown exactly as PlayStation publishes them; every guide below is written in our own words for this entry.
hiddenNote: Hidden flags follow the visible / hidden split published by OutputLag's trophy list (27 visible, 28 hidden): the 12 story trophies, the 5 side-story finales, Fair Game, and the 10 cryptic one-off trophies are hidden on PlayStation until earned.
sourcesNote: Each trophy lists its sources by id. The source directory (names and links) lives in app/src/sources.js and is shown beside every guide in the app.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: There is no separate task here: earn the other 54 trophies and this one pops on its own. Treat it as the finish line, not a job. In practice the last ones to fall are the gold for 100% completion (A Long Road) and the long grinds — 250 stunts, 42 gold shooting-range medals and the collectibles — so plan your route around those, and use this tracker's roadmap tab to see what is left.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, and finish it. This is an unmissable story trophy: it pops when the mission ends, so there is nothing to prepare and nothing that can go wrong. If it does not pop at once, keep playing — chapter trophies are sometimes awarded as the next chapter begins.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 1 of the story. Unmissable: every story mission in the chapter has to be completed in order, and the trophy follows. Two things matter while you are here, though. First, do Lucia's balcony meditation before the chapter ends — it counts toward Positive Mental Attitude and is gone afterwards. Second, keep a manual save from the start of the chapter: the game has no mission replay, so a save is your only way back.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2 of the story. Unmissable, like every chapter trophy. This chapter is where the wider game opens up: switching between Jason and Lucia becomes available here, which is what makes the partner trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy, Personal Best) possible, and the Scooter Bros app opens through the mission Moses, which starts On the Spot.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3 of the story. Unmissable. While you are in this chapter, watch for Race Against Yago in Yago's street-racing strand: it is time-sensitive (shown with an hourglass icon) and the strand counts toward Strangers & Freaks, so save first and race the moment it appears. The Chapter 3 mission Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs also hands you the Snap Gun, which opens jewelry-store robberies for Sneakthief.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4 of the story. Unmissable. Near the end of this chapter the optional mission That's Where The Money Is opens bank-vault robberies, so the robbery trophies (Maximum Withdrawal, Hot Together, A Classic Blitz Play) become available here. Keep a manual save from the start of the chapter, as you should for every chapter.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final mission of the story. Unmissable and the only gold trophy tied to the story itself. Before you start it, make a manual save you do not overwrite: there is no mission replay and no New Game Plus, so that save is your only way back to the end of the game. Everything outside the story — side-story finales, collectibles and the 100% checklist — stays available after the credits.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Breakfast Run. Unmissable: story missions are completed in order and the trophy pops at the mission's end. There is no special preparation and no way to miss it — just play the story through.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission The Cartel Heist. Unmissable: it pops when the mission ends. Heist missions in this game are story beats, not optional jobs — the optional robbery trophies (bank vaults, armored trucks, jewelry stores) are separate, and they open up in Chapters 3 and 4.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Child's Play. Unmissable: play the story in order and the trophy follows the mission. No preparation, no alternate route, nothing to miss.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Headliners. Unmissable: it pops at the end of the mission. The name is the mission's own title, which is why this trophy is hidden on PlayStation until you earn it — the spoiler setting in this tracker hides story trophies like this one until they pop.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission VCIA Takedown at Vice City International Airport. Unmissable. The airport matters again later: Catch Me If You Can asks you to steal a large passenger plane from a boarding bridge here (gates E3 and E4 are reported to work), so you will already know the layout when you come back for it.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Operation Savage Glory. Unmissable: the last of the named story-mission trophies, earned by playing the campaign in order. With the chapter trophies and the final mission, that is all twelve story trophies — the rest of the list is side content, collectibles, activities and grinds.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion. This is the hardest trophy on the list and the one that decides the platinum, so treat everything else as preparation for it. The 100% checklist itself only appears after the story, under Progress, Stats, 100% Completion — but work you do earlier still counts, so do not wait. The checklist is known to want 300 stunts (past the 250 of Cunning Stunts), 70 of the 80 Challenges, 200 of the 277 vehicle models, all 8 bank vaults and all 39 illegal operations. Check the in-game list once it appears and let it, not this guide, be the final word on what is left.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. Stunt jumps, flights under bridges, knife-edge flights and base jumps all count toward the same total, so use whichever you find while travelling instead of hunting one kind. Do not stop at 250 if you want the platinum: 100% completion needs 300 stunts, so keep the counter running past this trophy. Use this tracker's count box to log your PSN progress (0/250) as it grows.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once. PlayStation tracks this one as a count (0/9), so the game itself knows what counts — try one of every activity the map and menus offer (races, shooting range, fishing, arcade, bowling, meditation, gym training, drone racing and similar) and watch the counter move. Which exact nine the game counts has not yet been checked in the game, so this guide does not guess the list: play broadly, and the trophy pops when the ninth type registers.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. There are two shooting ranges with 42 gold medals between them, so you need gold on every challenge at both — a silver or bronze medal on any one of them leaves the trophy locked. Work through the challenges one weapon or drill at a time and replay any that fall short of gold; there is no time limit on retries. Log your gold count in the tracker's count box as you go.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every one of the 14 locations. One win per location is what counts — winning fourteen races at the same spot does not move the counter. Visit each location, win its race, and move on; the tracker counts locations, not races, so tick them off as you clear each new place.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Different is the key word: replaying the same race twenty times does not count. Enter new events as you find them — street races, circuit races and any other race type the game offers — and keep a mental note of which you have already won. This pairs naturally with the Top Fun drone races, but those are a separate trophy with their own counter.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the game's activities, and Cal is the rival you meet through it: find a fishing challenge where Cal is the opponent and out-fish him. Where exactly Cal waits and which challenge triggers the head-to-head has not yet been checked in the game, so this guide does not invent a spot — play the fishing activity when it appears and take the challenge against Cal when it is offered.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game. Walk into an arcade, pick a cabinet and play it through to the end — starting a game and quitting halfway does not count. Any cabinet should do; pick the one you find easiest and finish it. Arcades are also one of the activity types that feed Master of None, so this trophy and that one can be earned together.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy. Andy's is a side-story strand: a chain of missions for one character that ends in a finale, and the trophy pops when that finale is done. Side-story finales stay available after the credits, so there is no deadline — but note that Andy's strand does not count toward Strangers & Freaks, because it has its own trophy. Finish it when you are ready, not because the counter needs it.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton. Like the other side-story finales, this one stays open after the story ends, so play it at your own pace. Follow Kenton's strand of missions to its end and the trophy pops with the finale. There is no missable step here — the only thing to avoid is assuming the strand is finished before its final mission appears.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy. A side-story finale that stays available after the credits. Billy's strand, like Andy's and Tyrone's, does not count toward Strangers & Freaks — it has its own trophy instead — so do not expect double progress from it. Play the strand through to its last mission and the trophy follows.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.missableNote: At risk: the Chapter 3 race Race Against Yago in Yago's street-racing strand is time-sensitive (hourglass icon) and the strand counts toward this trophy. Save before it and race as soon as it appears. Also, Andy's, Billy's and Tyrone's strands do NOT count — they have their own trophies — so you need 8 other strands.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida. A strand is a whole chain of missions for one stranger, not a single job — finishing one strand moves the counter by one, and PlayStation tracks it as 0/8. Not every optional questline counts: Andy's, Billy's and Tyrone's strands have their own trophies and do not add to this one, so check the trophy's progress counter after each strand you finish. One strand race — Race Against Yago in Chapter 3 — is time-sensitive, so save first and race when it appears.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy. A side-story finale that stays available after the credits. Play Randy's strand through to its last mission and the trophy pops with the finale. Nothing about it is timed or missable — it is a matter of finding the strand and seeing it through.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone. A side-story finale that stays available after the credits. Tyrone's strand does not count toward Strangers & Freaks — it has its own trophy — so finish it for its own sake. Follow the strand to its final mission and the trophy follows.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.missableNote: MISSABLE — the one trophy every launch guide flags. Lucia's balcony meditation in Chapter 1 disappears once the chapter ends. Do it in Chapter 1 (after Lucia is home, check the kitchen in the morning — often the morning after the mission Down to Earth — follow her to the balcony and accept), and keep a Chapter 1 save until this trophy pops. It is not confirmed the balcony is strictly required, so do it anyway.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida — all 18 of them. Meditation spots show as purple icons when you are close, and each outdoor spot should count twice if you meditate there with both characters, so bring your partner every time. The one spot you can lose is Lucia's balcony meditation in Chapter 1: after Lucia is home, check the kitchen in the morning (often the morning after the mission Down to Earth), follow her out to the balcony of Jason's house and accept the optional task. It is gone once Chapter 1 ends, and it is not confirmed whether the trophy strictly needs it — so do it anyway and keep a Chapter 1 save until the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret Vogel's hunting questline is Jason-only and sends you after animals through target decks. Work through the questline until the unique animal is the target, then hunt it. A clean head or heart shot keeps the carcass pristine, which is what a hunting questline like this rewards. The questline stays available after the story, so there is no deadline.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are found across Leonida, and a set is complete when you hold every card in it — three finished sets is the trophy. Where each card sits has not yet been checked in the game, so this guide does not invent locations: collect cards as you explore, check your collection screen to see which sets are close, and finish the three nearest sets first. Nothing here is timed, and cards stay collectible after the credits.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK app at 100 locations. WAiNK is the in-game app for checking in at places: open it at a new location and check in, and the counter moves. A hundred different locations is the goal, so check in everywhere you go rather than saving it for a dedicated hunt. The same app also discovers vehicles — scanning traffic with WAiNK counts toward Whip It Good — so the two trophies progress together.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 Challenges. Challenges are listed under Progress, then Challenges, in the game's menu — open that list and work through it. Many complete on their own while you play, so check the list regularly instead of grinding them blind. Do not stop at 50 if you want the platinum: 100% completion needs 70 of the 80 Challenges.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star Wanted Level with your partner beside you and escape the heat. The easiest way to get four stars on demand is a bank-vault job, which gives you a 4-star Wanted Level straight away — and you need your partner along for the vault anyway. Escape together until you have left the red heat zone, not just the flashing search area: the trophy pops once you are truly clear. Switching between Jason and Lucia, and calling your partner in, opens during Chapter 2.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner, without losing your Wanted Level. Call your partner first, then rob three shops in a row while the police are still chasing you. The chain breaks if the stars fade and you are left in only the red heat zone — keep the wanted level alive between shops. The trophy can take about 30 seconds to pop after you leave the third shop, so give it a moment before you hit a fourth.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Scanning a vehicle with the WAiNK app counts as discovering it, so scan traffic as you drive instead of trying to steal or buy a hundred cars. The counter is cumulative across the whole game. For the platinum, keep going: 100% completion needs 200 of the 277 base models, so keep scanning everything new you see.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-motion aim: press L3 and R3 while aiming. Pick a group of enemies — the guards at an illegal operation work well — and use an assault rifle so you can drop five before Focus runs out. Adrenaline extends Focus, so use it if you have it. One clean run is all it takes; if you fall short, find another group and try again.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport: steal a large passenger plane that is docked at a boarding bridge. The planes at gates E3 and E4 are reported to work; planes parked elsewhere on the airfield do not count. Get up to the cockpit, back out toward the runway and take off, then fly about 1 km away from the airport — the trophy is delayed and pops once you are clear. Save first, because the police come fast.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Get into a Rhino tank — that is what the description's joke means by 'these Rhinos'. Tanks are reported to be parked on the south side of Mile Zero Air Station, on the island at the far southwest of the map. Save first, get in, and drive and fire until the trophy pops. Expect heavy police attention the moment you move, so do not plan a long drive.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. The Chapter 3 mission Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs gives you the Snap Gun and opens jewelry-store robberies — do that mission first. Use the Snap Gun on a store's locked back door: kicking the door in sets off the alarm. Inside the back room, find the note with the safe code, open the safe and leave without being seen. Richardson Jewelry & Diamonds in Vice City is a good target. If someone spots you, reload the save rather than pushing on.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape. Vaults open through the optional mission That's Where The Money Is near the end of Chapter 4: tail an armored security van to a large bank and get into the vault while the guard has it open. Bring your partner — you cannot carry all the bags alone. Each vault job gives you a 4-star Wanted Level straight away, so escaping one with your partner also earns Hot Together. The 100% checklist needs all 8 vaults, so keep going past five.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Ambush a truck on the road, take its cargo and get clear. Like the vault jobs, the trophy is about the escape as much as the robbery: get out of the red heat zone, not just out of sight, before you relax. Save before you try it, and use a fast car parked nearby for the getaway.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. Drive, fly and sail through every named area on the map until the counter reads 52 — PlayStation tracks it as 0/52, so the game itself knows which areas are left. Work through the map region by region rather than wandering, and use a plane or helicopter for the far corners and islands. Nothing here is timed or missable.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs — one per gang is enough for the trophy. Illegal operations are the gang-run spots you can rob across Leonida. The 100% checklist wants all 39 operations, so this trophy pops along the way if you keep robbing them; but if you want it early, make sure you spread your robberies across different gangs instead of hitting the same gang's spots nine times.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. The description is the whole instruction: find a bar with a view on Ocean Beach and order a cocktail there. Which bar counts has not yet been checked in the game, so this guide does not name one — walk the Ocean Beach front, look for a bar with a sea view, and order a drink. It is a small moment trophy, not a grind, and it cannot be missed.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style: drive a car through the showroom's front and out onto the street. Which showroom counts has not yet been checked in the game, so this guide does not name one — find a vehicle showroom you can drive into, get in a car inside, and go out through the glass. Save first, because the police will not love it.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. The alley is Kingpin Bowling, an illegal operation you visit in Chapter 2. Bring Sticky Bombs and take all three key valuables: the luxury watch in an office, the shotgun on a table, and the contents of the office safe, which you blow open with a Sticky Bomb. Then escape the police. If you leave something behind, the operation comes back later, so this one is not missable.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Reach maximum Strength with both Jason and Lucia together. Buy a gym membership and train with your partner there — your partner trains alongside you, so both characters build Strength in the same sessions. Keep training until both are at maximum and the trophy pops. Partner play opens during Chapter 2, and the gym is a normal activity, so there is no deadline.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make 500 choices that change your Criminal Profile. PlayStation tracks this one as a count (0/500), and it fills up through normal play: robberies, fights and other actions that shift your profile all feed it. There is no separate grind to plan — play the game, rob and fight as the story and side content ask you to, and check the counter now and then. If it is short near the end, a few more robberies will close the gap.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Succeed on a second try. The description is deliberately cryptic and no confirmed trigger is published yet — launch-era guides mark this one as not yet known. The honest reading is that it pops when something you failed once works the second time around. Do not chase it: play normally, retry what you fail, and let it pop. This guide will not invent a trigger for a trophy nobody has pinned down yet.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange somewhere in Leonida. The description is the whole hint, and no confirmed trigger is published yet — launch-era guides mark this one as not yet known. It is most likely a rare encounter or odd event in the open world, so explore widely and keep an eye out for anything out of place. Do not chase it with a made-up route: this guide says plainly that the trigger is unconfirmed, and the trophy is not missable.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by: hit a target with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. The exact setup has not yet been checked in the game, so this guide does not invent the details — the name says bowling, the description says a melee drive-by, and the practical reading is a melee swing from a slow-moving car at a pedestrian target. Try it in a quiet street, save first, and do not treat any single attempt as the confirmed method until the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from bank and payday-loan jobs; sell them to your contacts to launder them, and the total is cumulative — it does not have to be $250,000 in one go. Keep doing vault and payday jobs, launder what you take, and the counter climbs. Log your running total in the tracker's count box.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. The total is cumulative across every kind of shop — clothes, weapons, food, whatever the game sells — so it fills up through normal play. If you are short near the end, buy the expensive things you actually want (weapons and vehicles add up fast) rather than throwing money away. Check the counter in the tracker as you go.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties. Buy them in the Vice City Real Estate app, which unlocks after the Chapter 2 mission Daily Driver. Together they cost about $160,000, so save for them — and note that garages the story gives you do not count toward the eight. Buy garages early as well as late: each one gives you the free space you need to register cars for On the Spot.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The Chapter 2 mission Moses opens the app: take a stolen car to Moses, choose Respray, then Register. From Chapter 3 you can also register cars with a standard tracker at Pay 'n' Spray. Each car needs a free garage space, so buy garages first (Little Boxes) and register cheap cars you do not mind keeping.
